speaker: Unknown
en: LLMs, if you talk to them, they're incredibly intelligent.
zh: 大语言模型，如果你和它们对话，它们聪明得惊人。

speaker: Unknown
en: Their performance is insane.
zh: 它们的表现令人难以置信。

speaker: Unknown
en: But then you haven't seen that kind of impact on the physical world.
zh: 但你还没看到它们对物理世界产生那样的影响。

speaker: Unknown
en: Why is that?
zh: 为什么会这样？

speaker: Unknown
en: Our goal is to build a system that can intentionally synthesize matter.
zh: 我们的目标是构建一个能够有意识地合成物质的系统。

speaker: Unknown
en: This isn't going to emerge just from reading textbooks.
zh: 这不会仅仅靠阅读教科书就能涌现出来。

speaker: Unknown
en: It's really necessary to use simulations, model the physical world, but then actually carry out the experiments.
zh: 真正必要的是使用模拟，对物理世界建模，然后实际开展实验。

speaker: Unknown
en: If we are successful with periodic, it will actually increase the number of scientists in the world.
zh: 如果我们在 Periodic 上取得成功，实际上会增加世界上科学家的数量。

speaker: Unknown
en: Maybe let's get really granular to understand how this all comes together.
zh: 也许让我们深入到非常细的层面，来理解这一切是如何组合在一起的。

speaker: Unknown
en: Anyone could go into a lab and mix a bunch of powders and say they ran a lot of experiments.
zh: 任何人都可以走进实验室，混合一堆粉末，然后说自己做了很多实验。

speaker: Unknown
en: However, if you're not seeing what you're doing, there's no error correction loop, there's no intentionality to it.
zh: 然而，如果你没有观察到你正在做的事情，就没有纠错回路，也没有意图性可言。

speaker: Unknown
en: And so those are some of the first AI systems we had to build.
zh: 所以这些是我们必须构建的第一批 AI 系统之一。

speaker: Unknown
en: What we're targeting now are areas where the frontier is just not sufficient or we can do it vastly cheaper.
zh: 我们现在瞄准的是那些前沿能力还不够充分、或者我们可以以极其便宜得多的成本做到的领域。

speaker: Unknown
en: A system that can literally engineer matter is going to be of key importance to everybody.
zh: 一个能够真正工程化物质的系统，对每个人都将是至关重要的。

speaker: Unknown
en: If you had unlimited resources and no operational constraints, what is an experiment you'd really like to run?
zh: 如果你有无限的资源、没有任何运营限制，你最想做一个什么实验？

speaker: Unknown
en: I would love to see... AI has gotten very good at writing software.
zh: 我很想看到……AI 已经非常擅长编写软件了。

speaker: Unknown
en: That's no accident.
zh: 这绝非偶然。

speaker: Unknown
en: After all, code has an answer key a computer can check in a fraction of a second.
zh: 毕竟，代码有一份计算机可以在几分之一秒内核对的答案。

speaker: Unknown
en: The program either runs or it doesn't.
zh: 程序要么能运行，要么不能。

speaker: Unknown
en: Physics has an answer key too, the physical world.
zh: 物理学也有一份答案，那就是物理世界。

speaker: Unknown
en: But consulting it means running actual experiments, something an AI model can't do on its own.
zh: 但查询这份答案意味着进行真实的实验，而这是 AI 模型自己无法做到的。

speaker: Unknown
en: Liam Fedus and Doj Chubuk are building a company to change that.
zh: Liam Fedus 和 Doj Chubuk 正在创办一家公司来改变这一点。

speaker: Unknown
en: They're the founders of Periodic Labs, a startup building infrastructure to create what they call synthetic superintelligence.
zh: 他们是 Periodic Labs 的创始人，这家初创公司正在构建基础设施，以创造他们所说的合成超级智能。

speaker: Unknown
en: Liam previously led post-training at OpenAI and was one of the creators of ChatGPT, while Doge was a research scientist at Google DeepMind.
zh: Liam 此前在 OpenAI 领导后训练，并且是 ChatGPT 的缔造者之一，而 Doge 曾是 Google DeepMind 的研究科学家。

speaker: Unknown
en: They've brought their experience together to build what might be described as an AI scientist, capable of conducting thousands of experiments a day and learning from each one of them.
zh: 他们把各自的经验汇聚到一起，构建一个可以被描述为 AI 科学家的东西，它每天能够进行数千个实验，并从每一个实验中学习。

speaker: Unknown
en: In this episode, we discuss the limits of LLMs, why science is so hard, and what Liam learned from launching ChatGPT.
zh: 在本期节目中，我们讨论大语言模型的局限、为什么科学如此困难，以及 Liam 从发布 ChatGPT 中学到的东西。

speaker: Unknown
en: I'm Mario, and this is The Generalist.
zh: 我是 Mario，这里是 The Generalist。

speaker: Unknown
en: I'm really excited to have you both here.
zh: 我真的很高兴你们两位能来到这里。

speaker: Unknown
en: I've been really looking forward to this conversation.
zh: 我一直非常期待这次对话。

speaker: Unknown
en: I think you're building such a fascinating company.
zh: 我认为你们正在打造一家非常迷人的公司。

speaker: Unknown
en: So maybe we just start there.
zh: 那么也许我们就从这里开始。

speaker: Unknown
en: Tell me a little bit about Periodic.
zh: 跟我讲讲 Periodic 吧。

speaker: Unknown
en: What are you trying to do?
zh: 你们想做什么？

speaker: Unknown
en: Our goal is to build a system that can intentionally synthesize matter.
zh: 我们的目标是构建一个能够有意识地合成物质的系统。

speaker: Unknown
en: So we're calling this a synthesis superintelligence.
zh: 所以我们把它称为合成超级智能。

speaker: Unknown
en: Our core belief is in order to do this, you need to make connection with the real world.
zh: 我们的核心信念是，要做到这一点，你必须与真实世界建立连接。

speaker: Unknown
en: So a system like this isn't going to emerge just from reading textbooks, reading papers.
zh: 所以这样一个系统不会仅仅靠阅读教科书、阅读论文就能涌现出来。

speaker: Unknown
en: It's really necessary to use simulations.
zh: 真正必要的是使用模拟。

speaker: Unknown
en: Model the physical world, but then actually carry out the experiments.
zh: 对物理世界建模，然后实际开展实验。

speaker: Unknown
en: We kind of talk about like thinkism is not enough.
zh: 我们有种说法是，光靠思考是不够的。

speaker: Unknown
en: It's really necessary to get the new information from the world to conjecture how it might be, get the experiments back, and do this end-to-end loop.
zh: 真正必要的是从世界获取新信息， conjecture 猜想它可能是怎样的，拿回实验结果，并完成这个端到端的回路。

speaker: Unknown
en: By doing this end-to-end training against the physical world, new types of intelligence and AI systems will emerge.
zh: 通过针对物理世界进行这种端到端的训练，将会涌现出新类型的智能和 AI 系统。

speaker: Unknown
en: So rather than a system that has just been trained on the body of final scientific literature, it's been trained on the scientific process itself.
zh: 所以，它不是一个仅仅在最终科学文献的集合上训练出来的系统，而是在科学过程本身上训练出来的。

speaker: Unknown
en: So rather than knowing the state of science, it knows how to do science.
zh: 所以它不是知道科学的状态，而是知道如何做科学。

speaker: Unknown
en: I've heard one way that you've maybe described the mission in the past is almost to build an AI scientist, right?
zh: 我听说你们过去描述这个使命的一种方式，几乎是打造一个 AI 科学家，对吧？

speaker: Unknown
en: And decomposing the different pieces of that puzzle through that sort of lens.
zh: 并且通过那样的视角来拆解这个谜题的不同部分。

speaker: Unknown
en: How do you think about, you know, fundamentally, what does a scientist do and what do you need to replicate?
zh: 你是怎么思考的，从根本上说，科学家做什么？你需要复制的是什么？

speaker: Unknown
en: The traditional way to look at science is to say you come up with a hypothesis and then based on the hypothesis you do some experiments and the experiments either validate the hypothesis or invalidate it and then you update your hypothesis.
zh: 看待科学的传统方式是说，你提出一个假设，然后基于这个假设做一些实验，实验要么验证这个假设，要么推翻它，然后你更新你的假设。

speaker: Unknown
en: And I think what's really critical here for us is this observation that science always tries to change the boundary of our understanding.
zh: 而我认为这里对我们真正关键的是这样一个观察：科学总是试图改变我们理解的边界。

speaker: Unknown
en: Which by definition means it cannot just rely on what we already know because science is trying to figure out what we don't yet know.
zh: 而从定义上讲，这意味着它不能仅仅依赖我们已经知道的东西，因为科学正是在试图弄清楚我们还不知道的东西。

speaker: Unknown
en: And this is almost at odds with the traditional description of machine learning where machine learning trains on a training set and does well on a test set that has the same distribution as the training set.
zh: 这几乎与传统机器学习的描述相悖，传统机器学习是在训练集上训练，然后在与训练集具有相同分布的测试集上表现良好。

speaker: Unknown
en: So there's like a clear tension between what we call machine learning and what we call science.
zh: 所以在我们所说的机器学习和我们所说的科学之间存在明显的张力。

speaker: Unknown
en: And that's where we're basically trying to make progress.
zh: 这基本上就是我们试图取得进展的地方。

speaker: Unknown
en: And how have humans gotten around this problem, right?
zh: 那么人类是如何绕过这个问题的，对吧？

speaker: Unknown
en: Because at the end of the day, humans are also machine learning algorithms and they often have figured out things that they didn't know before.
zh: 因为归根结底，人类也是机器学习算法，而且他们常常搞明白了他们以前不知道的事情。

speaker: Unknown
en: And they had to iterate, like they had to run experiments or they had to write down a theory, get yelled at by reviewers and then updated.
zh: 而他们必须迭代，比如他们必须做实验，或者必须写下一个理论，被审稿人骂一顿，然后更新。

speaker: Unknown
en: You know, Einstein had to do this, Bardeen had to do this.
zh: 你知道，爱因斯坦不得不这样做，巴丁也不得不这样做。

speaker: Unknown
en: So we feel like LLM will have to do it too.
zh: 所以我们觉得 LLM 也将不得不这样做。

speaker: Unknown
en: So we've been trying to spend a lot of time and focus on building labs that can have an LLM and simulation iterate with it.
zh: 所以我们一直花大量时间和精力去构建能让 LLM 和仿真进行迭代的实验室。

speaker: Unknown
en: That's kind of our goal, yeah.
zh: 这就是我们的目标，是的。

speaker: Unknown
en: Liam, you mentioned sort of this idea of thinkism.
zh: Liam，你提到过一种叫 thinkism 的想法。

speaker: Unknown
en: For folks that maybe don't know what that really means, maybe you can tell us a little bit about it and parse the differentiation a bit there.
zh: 对于可能不太清楚这真正含义的人来说，也许你可以给我们讲一讲，并解析一下其中的区别。

speaker: Unknown
en: Yeah, I mean, I think it's this concept that an AI that just thinks for a very long time, maybe if you extrapolate out the inference tokens well beyond anything we've seen, it can just do anything.
zh: 是的，我的意思是，我认为这个概念是，一个只需思考非常长时间的 AI，也许如果你把推理 token 外推到远超我们所见过的任何程度，它就可以做任何事情。

speaker: Unknown
en: One of our deep scientific goals is to discover new high-temp superconductors.
zh: 我们的一个深层科学目标是发现新的高温超导体。

speaker: Unknown
en: And we don't think that a system trained in the way that they're trained today will think for a billion or a trillion tokens and suddenly intuit, here's a new high-temp superconductor.
zh: 而且我们不认为以今天这种训练方式训练出来的系统，会思考十亿或万亿个 token 后突然直观地领悟到：这里有一个新的高温超导体。

speaker: Unknown
en: We think that's just not in line with how we've pushed knowledge forward and science forward.
zh: 我们认为这与我们推进知识和科学的方式根本不符。

speaker: Unknown
en: And so I think that's kind of core to our belief.
zh: 所以我认为这是我们信念的核心。

speaker: Unknown
en: It's like you need to connect it to the physical world and iterate.
zh: 就是说你需要把它与物理世界连接起来并迭代。

speaker: Unknown
en: The data simply just doesn't exist, and that's how you're going to actually build new knowledge, not just rehash the existing knowledge.
zh: 数据根本就不存在，而这才是你真正构建新知识的方式，而不只是重复现有的知识。

speaker: Unknown
en: High-temperature superconductors, how did you land on that as sort of the right first step for this company?
zh: 高温超导体，你们是怎么把它确定为这家公司合适的第一步的？

speaker: Unknown
en: There are a couple of reasons.
zh: 有几个原因。

speaker: Unknown
en: Let me talk through a bunch of them.
zh: 让我逐一说一下。

speaker: Unknown
en: So as Liam said, our goal is synthesis superintelligence.
zh: 正如 Liam 所说，我们的目标是合成超级智能。

speaker: Unknown
en: And if we can synthesize anything in the lab, we might as well synthesize the most impactful thing, which is superconductors.
zh: 而如果我们能在实验室里合成任何东西，那我们不妨合成最具影响力的东西，也就是超导体。

speaker: Unknown
en: So that's one reason.
zh: 这是其中一个原因。

speaker: Unknown
en: Another reason is, imagine all the different sci-fi features you want to think of.
zh: 另一个原因是，想想你想得到的所有不同的科幻特性。

speaker: Unknown
en: They often involve superconductivity, like quantum computing, fusion, lossless transmission of energy.
zh: 它们常常涉及超导，比如量子计算、核聚变、能量的无损传输。

speaker: Unknown
en: These all have superconductors somewhere in there.
zh: 这些里面都有超导体。

speaker: Unknown
en: And the other thing is there's a sense in which superconductors are the most macroscale quantum mechanical phenomenon.
zh: 另一点是，在某种意义上，超导体是最宏观尺度的量子力学现象。

speaker: Unknown
en: There's something very fascinating about it.
zh: 这里面有一些非常迷人的东西。

speaker: Unknown
en: And if you think about the history of condensed matter physics, it goes through these seven year or so cycles of what's very popular and then it falls out.
zh: 而且如果你回顾凝聚态物理的历史，它大约每七年左右经历这样的周期：某个方向很热门，然后又失宠。

speaker: Unknown
en: There was topological insulators, heavy fermion physics.
zh: 曾经有拓扑绝缘体、重费米子物理。

speaker: Unknown
en: It kind of roughly matches the length of a PhD that these topics come up and down.
zh: 这些话题的起落周期大致与一个博士的时长相符。

speaker: Unknown
en: Superconductivity is one topic that never went out of the road.
zh: 而超导是一个从未出局的课题。

speaker: Unknown
en: You know, like, since its discovery by Ones back in 1910, people have been fascinated by it since, and we're still fascinated by it.
zh: 你知道，自从 Ones 在 1910 年发现它以来，人们一直对它着迷，我们至今仍然着迷。

speaker: Unknown
en: And it's also in the pursuit of this, you have to build up such sophisticated simulation infrastructure, AI infrastructure.
zh: 而且在追求这个目标的过程中，你必须构建如此精密的仿真基础设施、AI 基础设施。

speaker: Unknown
en: And this has a huge amount of generality.
zh: 而这具有巨大的通用性。

speaker: Unknown
en: So it sort of gives you the right stair steps and also is this massively impactful...
zh: 所以它既给了你正确的阶梯，也是一个有巨大影响力的事情……

speaker: Unknown
en: Exactly.
zh: 没错。

speaker: Unknown
en: In the pursuit of this super ambitious goal, you build up a huge amount of incredibly impactful technology.
zh: 在追求这个超级宏大目标的过程中，你会积累大量极具影响力的技术。

speaker: Unknown
en: Doge, I've heard you mention Onus before.
zh: Doge，我听你以前提过 Onus。

speaker: Unknown
en: For folks who don't know that history, what they achieved, can you tell us a little bit about why they're an inspiration?
zh: 对于不了解那段历史、不了解他们成就的人来说，你能给我们讲讲为什么他们是一种激励吗？

speaker: Unknown
en: Yeah, absolutely.
zh: 是的，当然。

speaker: Unknown
en: Because honest is an inspiration to us in many ways.
zh: 因为 honest 在很多方面对我们是一种激励。

speaker: Unknown
en: So this is a good thing to talk about.
zh: 所以这是一个值得谈的话题。

speaker: Unknown
en: So in the 1800s, there was a big rush to liquefy as many of the gases as possible.
zh: 在 19 世纪，有一场把尽可能多的气体液化的热潮。

speaker: Unknown
en: So I think around 1850, they liquefied oxygen, for example, and ended up playing a big role in industry.
zh: 我想大约在 1850 年，他们液化氧气，举例来说，最终在工业中发挥了重要作用。

speaker: Unknown
en: So they were trying to kind of go down in the periodic table and liquefy as many of the gases as possible.
zh: 所以他们试图沿着元素周期表往下走，把尽可能多的气体液化。

speaker: Unknown
en: As you can imagine, you have to lower the temperature more and more.
zh: 可以想象，你必须把温度降得越来越低。

speaker: Unknown
en: Helium was the hardest one because, you know, it's a noble gas.
zh: 氦是最难的一个，因为，你知道，它是一种惰性气体。

speaker: Unknown
en: So it doesn't really interact with other atoms very strongly, which means this liquefaction temperature will be low.
zh: 所以它与其他原子的相互作用不是很强，这意味着它的液化温度会比较低。

speaker: Unknown
en: And helium, especially among the noble gases, is the smallest one.
zh: 而氦，尤其是在惰性气体中，是最小的那一个。

speaker: Unknown
en: So that was the last one to be tackled.
zh: 所以它是最后一个被攻克的。

speaker: Unknown
en: And Annes built a lab to go after this.
zh: AnneS 建了一个实验室来攻克这个问题。

speaker: Unknown
en: And one of his very interesting ideas was that science should be done at an industrial scale by professionals.
zh: 他的一个非常有趣的想法是，科学应该由专业人士以工业化的规模来做。

speaker: Unknown
en: So he would hire professional technicians, professional engineers to work in a science lab, which was, I think, a bit like funny at the time to people.
zh: 所以他会雇用专业的技术员、专业的工程师在科学实验室里工作，我觉得这在当时的人们看来有点好笑。

speaker: Unknown
en: And he succeeded.
zh: 而且他成功了。

speaker: Unknown
en: So, you know, after a lot of hard work and he had a large team doing it, he was able to liquefy helium.
zh: 你知道，经过大量的艰苦工作，而且他有一个很大的团队在做这件事，他成功地液化了氦。

speaker: Unknown
en: And interestingly, you know, he got the Nobel Prize for liquefying helium.
zh: 有趣的是，你知道，他是因为液化氦而获得诺贝尔奖的。

speaker: Unknown
en: He didn't get it for discovering superconductivity.
zh: 他并不是因为发现超导而获得诺贝尔奖的。

speaker: Unknown
en: So he just like basically created a new capability, which is lowering the temperature to below 4 Kelvin.
zh: 所以他基本上就是创造了一种新能力，也就是把温度降到 4 开尔文以下。

speaker: Unknown
en: As you know, zero Kelvin is the absolute zero.
zh: 如你所知，0 开尔文是绝对零度。

speaker: Unknown
en: We don't expect to go any below that.
zh: 我们不指望能低于那个温度。

speaker: Unknown
en: And four Kelvin is really cold.
zh: 而 4 开尔文是非常冷的。

speaker: Unknown
en: But once he reached four Kelvin, he could go down a bit more to 1.8.
zh: 但一旦他达到了 4 开尔文，他就可以再往下降一点，降到 1.8。

speaker: Unknown
en: And then after he was able to do that, he knew that some people were wondering what would happen to metals if it got really cold.
zh: 然后在他能够做到这一点之后，他知道有些人在好奇，如果变得非常冷，金属会发生什么。

speaker: Unknown
en: And some really smart people like Lord Calvin thought that if you could go such low temperatures, electrons would basically freeze.
zh: 而一些非常聪明的人，比如 Lord Calvin,认为如果你能达到这么低的温度，电子基本上会冻结。

speaker: Unknown
en: And it's kind of intuitive, right?
zh: 这还挺符合直觉的，对吧？

speaker: Unknown
en: It's so cold, electrons don't want to move anymore.
zh: 天这么冷，电子就不再想动了。

speaker: Unknown
en: So he wanted to try it.
zh: 所以他想试一试。

speaker: Unknown
en: And I think one of his scientists there tried putting different metals into liquefied helium or like very cold temperature.
zh: 我觉得他那里的一位科学家试着把不同的金属放进液化氦里，或者说是非常冷的温度中。

speaker: Unknown
en: And one of the things they tried was mercury.
zh: 而他们尝试的东西之一就是水银。

speaker: Unknown
en: And it turns out mercury is a superconductor at such low temperatures.
zh: 结果发现，水银在这么低的温度下是一种超导体。

speaker: Unknown
en: And then once you observed that it was a big deal and that kind of opened up this whole area around superconductivity.
zh: 而一旦你观察到了这一点，那就是一件大事，这开启了围绕超导的整个领域。

speaker: Unknown
en: Thank you for that history.
zh: 谢谢你讲这段历史。

speaker: Unknown
en: That's very interesting.
zh: 非常有意思。

speaker: Unknown
en: You both mentioned this phrase, synthesis superintelligence.
zh: 你们两位都提到了这个词，synthesis superintelligence(合成式超级智能)。

speaker: Unknown
en: I'm sure folks have an understanding of what synthesis is, but, you know, why that word?
zh: 我相信大家对什么是 synthesis(合成)都有一定的理解，但是，你知道，为什么用这个词？
